title: Struct Pointers (->)
concept: A convenient arrow used to point to a structure.

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
Header for using `printf`.

This lesson covers how to modify the original by passing a structure as a pointer.

steps.title: Player structure definition
steps.explanation:
`Player` is a structure type that combines name and health.

It is the basic unit for handling related data as a single object.

steps.title: define heal function (using pointer)
steps.explanation:
`heal(struct Player *p)` receives and processes the address of the player structure.

Once you receive the address, you can directly modify the original member inside the function.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created and prepares the player instance.

steps.title: Create structure variable
steps.explanation:
Set the initial name and health to the `warrior` variable.

This value becomes the reference state before calling the function.

steps.title: Initial stamina output
steps.explanation: Prints the physical strength before calling and records the state before the change.

steps.title: call heal function (pass address)
steps.explanation:
Pass the structure address to `heal(&warrior)`.

Changes are reflected by passing the original location rather than a copy.

steps.title: Method 1: Dereference followed by dot operator
steps.explanation: You can access members with the dot operator after dereferencing them like `(*p).hp`.

steps.title: Method 2: Arrow operator (->)
steps.explanation:
`p->hp` is an abbreviation with the same meaning as `(*p).hp`.

This notation is usually used for pointer member access.

steps.title: Check your changed stamina
steps.explanation:
If you check the health after calling the function, the original value has actually changed.

It shows that pointer passing led to modification of the original.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Key point: When passing a structure pointer, member access is `->` by default.

quiz.question: struct A *ptr; What is the correct way to access member x when
quiz.explanation:
Since it is a pointer, you must use an arrow (`->`).
`ptr.x` is used only when ptr is a structure variable.
`*ptr.x` becomes `*(ptr.x)` due to operator precedence, which is incorrect syntax.

misconceptions.correct: This is a fundamental feature of the C language.
misconceptions.why: This is a shortcut created because structure pointer access is too frequent.

keyTakeaway: For structure pointers, use `->` instead of `.`.
